# Code of Conduct

The iTrack Zimbabwe community is committed to a respectful, professional, and inclusive collaboration environment.

## Expected behavior

- Communicate respectfully and assume good intent while remaining open to correction.
- Give actionable feedback focused on the code, documentation, behavior, or proposal rather than the person.
- Welcome different backgrounds, experience levels, viewpoints, and communication styles.
- Keep discussions relevant, constructive, and safe for a professional open-source project.
- Respect privacy and never publish credentials, personal data, production records, or private correspondence.

## Unacceptable behavior

Harassment, discrimination, threats, personal attacks, intimidation, sexualized conduct, hate speech, deliberate disruption, doxxing, and publication of private information are not acceptable. Attempts to bypass security controls, expose secrets, or abuse project infrastructure may also be treated as conduct violations.

## Scope and enforcement

This code applies to project spaces, issues, pull requests, code reviews, discussions, documentation, and project-related events or communications. Maintainers may edit or remove content, close discussions, limit participation, or reject contributions when behavior violates this standard. Serious or repeated violations may result in a permanent ban from project spaces.

Report conduct concerns privately to the project maintainers. Security vulnerabilities should follow the private process in the [Security Guide](../docs/SECURITY.md), not a public issue.
